locator: VIII.6, Ita quod notum est Dei, manifestauit eis ipse, cum ab eis inuisibilia eius per ea, quae facta sunt, intellecta conspecta sunt
interpretation: VIII.6: the philosophers 'uiderunt esse aliquid ubi prima esset incommutabilis ... atque ibi esse rerum principium rectissime crediderunt, quod factum non esset et ex quo facta cuncta essent. Ita quod notum est Dei, manifestauit eis ipse, cum ab eis inuisibilia eius per ea, quae facta sunt, intellecta conspecta sunt'. Augustine applies Rom 1:19-20 to pagan Platonists; he credits their reasoning (from changeability of forms), and says God showed it to them.
attribution: The passage states that the Platonist philosophers, reasoning from the changeability of bodily and mental forms, saw an unchangeable first principle by which all things were made, and that God thus showed them what is known of him through the things made, which is the premise.
